> **These notes are unfinished intentionally.** They reflect what we have actually done so far and will grow from student contributions.

## What we covered

### Course routines and Name Tag V1

We started with a small communication problem: make it easier for people in the room to know who you are.

Even a simple name tag has requirements. It needs to communicate clearly before it can be decorative.

[Open the Day 1 slides](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1p0yf6PA4mhSOfAxJ19wpXhxePFQx4kz5Jz4989cHkOU/edit?usp=drivesdk)

### Personal identity

The About Me work asked what you would want another person to understand about you.

We used identity, experiences, interests, communities, skills, and goals as material for communication.

[Open the Day 2 slides](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1rIvj40b5GO1Xzyo0S38Cm4R6WesIWgqj6C-eGYEG2Q8/edit?usp=drivesdk)

### Listening and learning about other people

We practised listening while classmates presented and recording what we learned.

[Open the Day 3 slides](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1FkCCxUMBeYAQexZACz91rfpqw9DYzpc_vCTU3fVtXhA/edit?usp=drivesdk)

### Technical description and communication

We then moved toward describing things clearly enough that another person could understand the object, system, or idea.

Technical work depends on communication that another person can follow.

[Open the Day 4 slides](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1R2MjvtUzQPXqrCgDTu3L_wF46BSiIM5OyjBI7ysw0W0/edit?usp=drivesdk)

### Funday Friday: Machine Charades

We used machine charades as a low-stakes communication activity. The goal was to represent a machine or process clearly without depending only on spoken explanation.

## From personal identity to group identity

Technical teams also develop identities through shared:

- language
- routines
- expectations
- symbols
- visual conventions
- ways of solving problems

This gives us a bridge from personal identity to group identity and later to visual communication.
